To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the anti-prolific activity of EVO, RUT in 2D and 3D multicell spheroids was evaluated and the cellular uptake and fluorescence of EVO, and RUT were measured in 2D models.

the anti-prolific activity and cellular uptake were evaluated for EVO and Rutaecarphine in 3D tumor models and the results indicated that 3D multicelluar spheroids could better mimic the in vivo situation than 2D monlauyers and the cellular uptake was characterized by the fluorescence of EVO.

the anti-prolificative activity of EVO, and RUT was significantly increased from 2D to 3D models and the cellular uptake concentrations increased with increasing RUT concentrations, but the EVO concentrations showed only a small increase with increasing EVO concentrations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the anti-proliperative activity of EVO, RUT and the cellular uptake in 3D tumor models.
the anti-proliperation activity and cellular uptake evaluation of EVO and rut in 3D tumor models.
the application of 3D tumor models and the fluorescence of compounds for evaluating the cellular uptake and anti-tumor activity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the 3D multicell spheroids can better reflect the in vivo response of the tumor to the treatment, and the fluorescence of the drug is a useful method to evaluate the cellular uptake of EVD and RUT in the cells.
3D tumor models can better reflect an in vitro response to the treatment than 2D tumor monolayers.
EVO and Rutaecapine are effective in 2D cell monolayers, while their anti-proliferation activities are decreased in 3D tumor models.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cellular uptake concentration and fluorescence of EVO were higher than those of RUT.
the 3D multicellar tumor models are more appropriate for the anti-tumor evaluation of EVO and/or RUT.
the 3D multicelluar spheroids can be used as a more realistic model to study the anti-tumor effects of EVO and other drugs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the 3D multicell tumor model can be used for drug screening and evaluation.
the 3D multicell spheroid model can be applied in the evaluation of the anti-tumoral effect and cellular uptake of the drugs.
the anti-tumor activities of EVO and rut in 3D spheroids are weaker than that in 2D cultures, and the cellular uptake is also weaker than that in monolayers.
